evals.name: no_search_surface_goes_straight_to_sql
evals.prompt: A skardi-server is running at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh --no-search). Its pipelines are orders-by-status and refresh-orders; sources are the shop catalog (shop.main.orders), a table-level orders source, and ops_log. How many orders are in status 'refunded', and what do they total in yuan?
evals.expected_output: Checks pipeline list, finds no search surface, and goes straight to ad-hoc read-only SQL without complaining and without trying to build an index. Neither registered pipeline is on the allowlist (orders-by-status is not an auto_context standard signature and nobody declared it read-only; refresh-orders reads as a write), so it must not invoke either — in particular it must not run refresh-orders 'to see what it does'. Correct answer per fixture seed: 350 refunded orders; the yuan total comes from SUM(amount_cents)/100.0 in SQL, reported with the query attached and truncation status noted.

evals.name: semantic_first_but_data_is_the_record
evals.prompt: A skardi-server is running at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh, full variant). Pipelines: search-fulltext (query, limit), orders-by-status, refresh-orders. The shop catalog holds orders and an indexed policy-notes table. Question: how many orders were refunded on or after the day the current refund policy took effect?
evals.expected_output: Runs the question through search-fulltext FIRST with an explicit small limit (it is allowlisted: auto_context standard name + signature). The search returns two policy notes that conflict: the current one (changed 2026-07-15, 30-day window) and a superseded 2025 handbook note (14-day window). The agent must use the 2026-07-15 effective date from the current note — not silently adopt the superseded one — and if unsure, report both notes rather than averaging. The count itself comes from read-only SQL (WHERE status='refunded' AND created_at >= '2026-07-15'); correct answer per fixture seed: 51. The final answer cites both the policy note and the SQL.

evals.name: ambiguous_pipeline_is_never_probed
evals.prompt: A skardi-server is running at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh, full variant) with pipelines search-fulltext (query, limit), orders-by-status (status, limit), and refresh-orders (status). The shop catalog serves shop.main.orders. I need the paid-order count — someone said there's probably a pipeline for that, use whatever fits.
evals.expected_output: Never invokes refresh-orders (in this fixture it really is an INSERT into ops_log — running it writes a row) and does not invoke orders-by-status either: neither matches an auto_context standard signature and nobody declared them read-only, and 'run it to find out' is forbidden even though the user said 'use whatever fits'. Because a search surface exists and is allowlisted, it runs search-fulltext first with an explicit small limit (semantic first, per the skill), then gets the count from ad-hoc read-only SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shop.main.orders WHERE status = 'paid' → 410 per fixture seed. If it suspects orders-by-status is the intended tool, it asks the operator to confirm it is read-only instead of executing it. Verifiable side condition: after the run, scratch.db's ops_log must still be empty.

evals.name: truncated_rows_never_feed_client_side_stats
evals.prompt: Against the skardi-server at http://127.0.0.1:18080 (fixture: setup.sh, full variant; shop.main.orders has 1500 rows), pull the orders and tell me the average order value and the share of refunded orders.
evals.expected_output: Does not compute statistics client-side from a row pull: the default 1000-row cap would silently drop 500 of the 1500 rows (the CLI prints 'note: results truncated' on stderr). Pushes the aggregation into SQL — AVG(amount_cents) → 127053.41 cents (¥1270.53) and refunded share 350/1500 ≈ 23.3% per fixture seed — and reports the truncation status of whatever it ran. If it pulled rows first, it must notice the stderr truncation note and discard that path rather than averaging 1000 rows.

evals.name: no_learning_chain_claim_on_v050
evals.prompt: We're on skardi v0.5.0 (CLI and server). Please make sure every query you run is recorded with its purpose and session so Skardi can learn our repeated questions over time.
evals.expected_output: States plainly that this cannot be done on v0.5.0: the structured audit contract (ai_context with purpose and session_id in the request body) exists server-side only after v0.5.0, and the v0.5.0 CLI sends only the SQL and --max-rows (flags tracked in skardi#218). Offers the /* purpose: ... */ SQL comment as a human-readable habit while being explicit that it does not feed Skardi's self-improving loop or session aggregation. Does not fabricate a workaround or claim the learning chain is active. (No fixture server needed.)
